prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live listings from here, but I can tell you the fastest, most reliable ways to find certified backflow testers and repair techs near Liberty, MO — plus what to ask and typical costs so you can pick the right contractor.

Where to look
- Contact the City of Liberty Water/Public Works (they often keep a list of approved/certified backflow testers or can tell you reporting requirements).  
- Search Google Maps/Yelp/Angie’s List/HomeAdvisor for “backflow testing Liberty MO,” “backflow tester,” “backflow preventer repair,” “irrigation backflow testing,” or “fire protection backflow tester.”  
- Call local full‑service plumbers, irrigation companies, and fire protection contractors — they commonly do backflow testing and on‑site repairs.  
- Ask the Missouri Dept. of Natural Resources or your local water utility about backflow tester certification requirements and whether testers must be registered with the utility.

What to expect (pricing & timeline)
- Test only: commonly $50–$150 per device (varies by size/type).  
- Repairs/parts: can range from $50 for a simple repair to several hundred for replacement parts or larger assemblies. Full assembly replacement can be $400+ depending on size.  
- Fire system backflow assemblies and larger diameter devices cost more to test/repair and may require a specialist.  
- Most testers can perform same‑day testing and minor repairs; larger repairs may require ordering parts.

What to ask any contractor before you hire them
- Are you a certified backflow tester in Missouri? (Ask for their certification number and expiration.)  
- When was your test gauge last calibrated? (Gauge calibration is required.)  
- Do you handle both irrigation and fire protection backflow assemblies? (Fire backflows can need a different tester.)  
- Will you file/submit the test report to the city/water utility, or do I need to?  
- Do you provide a written test report and parts warranty?  
- Can you give an estimate for common repairs and parts?  
- Do you carry parts for on‑site repairs, and do you charge a trip fee?

How to compare bids
- Confirm they use a calibrated gauge and provide a signed test report.  
- Prefer technicians who will file the report with the city for you.  
- Get at least two quotes for repairs to compare parts and labor.  
- Check reviews and ask for references, especially for fire protection work.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short phone/email script you can use when calling providers.  
- Suggest search phrases and filtered results to paste into Google Maps/Yelp.  
- If you want me to try to find a list of local companies, tell me and I’ll search online (I’ll need permission to browse).
